note: The BIMobject User Terms/EULA restrict downloaded BIM Objects at the platform
level, not per product. Clauses 4.4(b), 4.7(f), 4.7(g) and 4.7(i) each
independently prohibit shipping any BIMobject-sourced asset in a publicly
distributed game. That determination is dispositive for every product on the
platform, so per-product evaluation cannot change the outcome and no product
files were downloaded for this wave.
Candidates are therefore recorded as CATEGORY CLASSES matching the wave brief's
search matrices, each carrying the same rights determination and each mapped to
the original clean-room Kaki kit that replaces it.
See docs/BIMOBJECT_PERMISSION_NOTES.md for the full clause analysis.

controllingClauses: 4.4(b) downloaded BIM Objects are for personal, non-commercial use only
4.7(f) no distribution or provision of access to third parties
4.7(g) no incorporation into a product or service provided to a third party
4.7(i) no removal or obscuring of proprietary notices, which forbids de-branding
rightsBasis.conclusion: Public GitHub Pages distribution of an MIT-licensed game, with a stated intent to preserve future commercial release, falls outside every permitted use purpose in section 4.4 and is expressly prohibited by 4.7(f) and 4.7(g).

candidateClasses.intendedKakiUse: Roadside containment along Off-Road GP venues and Draw Your Track safety dressing
candidateClasses.rightsRationale: EULA 4.4(b)/4.7(f)/4.7(g). Redistribution in a public game is prohibited regardless of product.
candidateClasses.protectabilityNote: Guardrail and barrier profiles are utilitarian forms dictated by function and by public highway standards; the Kaki substitute is modelled from generic engineering practice, not from any product.

candidateClasses.intendedKakiUse: Culverts, drainage channels and retaining walls for rural and quarry venues
candidateClasses.protectabilityNote: Pipe, culvert and channel sections are standard civil forms.

candidateClasses.intendedKakiUse: Whisker Yard freight and fabrication district dressing
candidateClasses.rightsRationale: EULA 4.4(b)/4.7(f)/4.7(g). Additionally many products in this category carry inseparable manufacturer branding, which 4.7(i) forbids removing.
candidateClasses.protectabilityNote: Dock, rack and stair forms are functional; Kaki versions use original proportions and the project's own decal language.

candidateClasses.searchMatrix: Kaki Stock Cup / Thunderbowl, Monster Smash
candidateClasses.intendedKakiUse: Thunderbowl short-track facility and Monster Smash event venue
candidateClasses.protectabilityNote: Tiered seating and catch fencing are standard venue forms.

candidateClasses.intendedKakiUse: Light masts, service lighting and utility dressing across all venues
candidateClasses.rightsRationale: EULA 4.4(b)/4.7(f)/4.7(g). This category is the most branding-dense on the platform; 4.7(i) independently blocks the de-branding step.
candidateClasses.protectabilityNote: Luminaire housings frequently carry protected ornamental design; Kaki masts use original chunky silhouettes consistent with the project art direction.

candidateClasses.category: Field, expedition and temporary event structures
candidateClasses.intendedKakiUse: Bivouac, timing and service infrastructure for desert stages
candidateClasses.protectabilityNote: Canopies, tanks and masts are functional forms. No branded fuel-dispensing equipment is recreated in any form.

candidateClasses.category: Site furniture, signage and event clutter
candidateClasses.intendedKakiUse: Shared race-day prop kit used by every mode
candidateClasses.rightsRationale: EULA 4.4(b)/4.7(f)/4.7(g). Traffic and directional signage additionally risks reproducing protected jurisdictional sign systems and third-party trademarks.
candidateClasses.protectabilityNote: All Kaki signage uses the project's fictional in-world sign language and carries no real-world manufacturer or jurisdiction marks.
